questions.stem: Why can graphite conduct electricity but diamond cannot?

options.text: Graphite contains ionic bonds while diamond contains covalent bonds
In graphite, each carbon bonds to only 3 others, leaving one delocalised electron per atom that can carry charge
Graphite is softer, which allows electricity to flow more easily
Diamond is transparent and light passes through instead of electricity

questions.explanation: In graphite, each carbon atom bonds to only 3 other carbon atoms, so one outer electron per carbon is not used in bonding. These electrons become delocalised and free to move through the structure, carrying electrical charge. In diamond, all 4 outer electrons are used in covalent bonds, so there are no free electrons.

options.text: It has weak intermolecular forces between its layers
Each carbon atom forms strong covalent bonds to 4 other carbon atoms in all directions
It contains metallic bonds that are very rigid
It is made of very large molecules packed tightly together

questions.explanation: Diamond is extremely hard because each carbon atom is bonded to 4 other carbon atoms by strong covalent bonds in a tetrahedral arrangement. These strong bonds extend in all directions throughout the giant covalent structure, making it very rigid and difficult to break.
